capabilities: Manager API inventory for agents, rules, decoders, and manager status
Rule and decoder analysis for alert-generation and log-parsing coverage
Indexer-backed alert search and evidence retrieval
interpretation: A Wazuh alert is a detection signal, not ground truth; corroborate it with endpoint, identity, network, and case evidence.
Custom rule identifiers should use the documented 100000-120000 range and custom files under /var/ossec/etc/rules/.
Test rule changes with wazuh-logtest and representative events before controlled replay or deployment.
configuration_checks: Confirm custom rules and decoders survive upgrades by keeping them outside the default ruleset directory.
Verify API permissions expose only the read operations required for assurance collection.
Review duplicate rule IDs, decoder availability, MITRE mappings, noisy rules, and missing telemetry from approved assets.
safety_constraints: Do not modify rules, decoders, agents, or index data from a recommendation.
Require approved replay evidence and a separate production change approval before deployment.

capabilities: Observable, task, comment, and case-template workflows
interpretation: Keep external TheHive IDs distinct from local case IDs and make synchronization idempotent.
Apply TLP and PAP markings to observables according to the organization's sharing policy.
configuration_checks: Review unassigned cases, incomplete alert-to-case flow, observable markings, case templates, and API permissions.
Use read-only collection for validation and separate approval-gated routes for writes.
safety_constraints: Case creation, updates, comments, and observable attachment are write actions and require explicit approval.

capabilities: Run analyzers against supported observable data types
Expose responders for approved response workflows
interpretation: Analyzer output is enrichment evidence and may be incomplete, stale, or conflicting; it does not independently prove maliciousness.
configuration_checks: Confirm analyzers and responders are enabled only for required organizations and observable types.
Validate analyzer secrets, timeouts, resource limits, and output handling without storing secret values.
safety_constraints: Analyzer execution and every responder action require scope checks and approval; responders remain disabled until explicitly enabled.

capabilities: Use taxonomies, warning lists, feeds, objects, and sharing controls
Export case intelligence as STIX and propose approval-gated MISP publication
interpretation: An indicator match is context, not proof of compromise; consider sighting age, confidence, distribution, warning lists, and local evidence.
configuration_checks: Review taxonomies, warning lists, feeds, sync servers, distribution, object templates, and API account permissions.
safety_constraints: Publishing attributes or events changes shared intelligence and requires explicit approval and an auditable preview.

capabilities: Retrieve file, URL, domain, and IP analysis and relationship data
interpretation: Engine detections and reputation are supporting evidence; review timestamps, engine consensus, relationships, and local context.
configuration_checks: Respect the selected API tier, quotas, data-sharing terms, and organization policy before submitting samples or URLs.
safety_constraints: Do not upload private files, URLs, or internal indicators unless policy explicitly permits external submission.

capabilities: Check IP abuse reports and confidence data
interpretation: Abuse confidence and report counts are reputation signals; shared infrastructure, NAT, VPNs, and data age can create misleading conclusions.
configuration_checks: Validate API quota handling, maximum-age selection, and redaction of internal addresses.
safety_constraints: Do not report an address to AbuseIPDB automatically; external reporting requires human approval and evidence.

capabilities: Retrieve observed internet-facing host and service metadata
interpretation: Shodan observations can be stale and do not prove current exposure; verify ownership, timestamps, and the live approved asset inventory.
configuration_checks: Constrain searches to approved assets and account for API plan limits.
safety_constraints: A lookup does not authorize active scanning; active tools require separate scope and approval checks.

capabilities: Search existing URL scan results and submit URLs when policy permits
interpretation: Search results and verdicts are enrichment; confirm scan visibility, collection time, redirects, and local telemetry.
configuration_checks: Default to searching existing results and verify API quotas and submission visibility settings.
safety_constraints: Submitting an internal or tokenized URL can disclose it externally; submission requires explicit approval.

capabilities: Search file hashes and retrieve sandbox analysis metadata
interpretation: Sandbox verdicts are supporting evidence; inspect behavioral detail, sample identity, environment, and analysis age.
configuration_checks: Validate API authentication, quotas, and the organization's sample-submission policy.
safety_constraints: The current integration performs hash search; sample upload must not be inferred or performed without separate approval.

capabilities: Check whether a URL appears in the PhishTank community database
interpretation: A database match supports a phishing assessment; no match does not establish that a URL is benign.
configuration_checks: Use the application key when available and handle service limits and unavailable results.
safety_constraints: Do not submit private URLs or phishing reports automatically.

capabilities: Provide organization-selected model inference through an API key or Codex CLI ChatGPT sign-in
interpretation: Model output is advisory and may be incomplete; ground recommendations in case evidence, approved architecture, and cited vendor context.
configuration_checks: Keep API-key and ChatGPT sign-in modes separate, select an approved model, and verify the Codex CLI login state on the application host.
safety_constraints: Never include secrets in prompts; model output cannot grant scope, approval, permissions, or production-change authority.
